tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description begins with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on the user's situation (patching blocked by repo access/auth failure), explicitly lists trigger contexts including exact error strings and mechanisms (RHUI cert expiry, subscription-manager lapse, GPG/TLS issues, proxy/time-skew), and notes it applies even when the user doesn't name the domain directly ('even when the user only says the repos are unreachable'). It is a dense but still concise paragraph covering scope thoroughly without drifting into internal implementation mechanics.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a Linux EC2 instance's patching is blocked by a repository access or authentication failure ... Use it when a patch run fails with "Failed to download metadata for repo" ... even when the user only says the repos are unreachable.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps straight into domain-specific fault classification (RHUI certs, subscription-manager, ULN, GPG) without explaining general concepts like what yum or GPG checks are. It stays tight and relevant throughout.
tests.evidence: RHUI client cert expired (RHEL PAYG): certs in /etc/pki/rhui/ are region-specific (~2-year validity).
